boxes.title: Jobs waiting in line
boxes.plain: Each accepted parcel is a row in the jobs table with status pending. A job can be claimed once its available_at time has passed, which is how backoff delays work.

boxes.title: Claim the oldest ready job
boxes.plain: One transaction picks the oldest pending job that is ready and returns it, or returns nothing if no job is ready.
boxes.why: Only one worker can lease a given job at a time.
outputs: a Job with a lease token, or nothing

boxes.title: Job leased to a worker
boxes.plain: While leased, the job belongs to one worker until lease_until (LEASE_SECONDS, 30 by default). Claiming also adds one to its attempts. Only the holder of the lease token can complete, fail or hold it.

boxes.title: Reclaim expired leases
boxes.plain: Before every claim, jobs whose lease ran out go back in line, or are failed if they already used their last attempt. A crashed worker's job is not lost.
boxes.why: A worker that dies mid-job must not strand it.
boxes.failure: Out of attempts: the job is failed with 'lease expired on final attempt'

boxes.title: Mark the job done
boxes.plain: Marks a leased job done and stores its carrier label. It only works for the current lease token; a worker whose lease expired and was re-claimed gets False and drops its result.
boxes.failure: False when the lease token no longer matches

boxes.title: Finished jobs
boxes.plain: Done jobs stay in the table. The report counts them as delivered, and the web client's wait stops when it sees one.

routes.why: Pending is a table state, not code: the worker reaches the job by claiming it on its next tick.
reclaim_expired found no leased row past its lease_until, so the pass goes on to claim.
An expired lease with attempts below MAX_ATTEMPTS goes back to pending, available now.
An expired lease on the final attempt is failed for good.
A pending row with available_at in the past exists; it is leased to this worker.
No pending row is ready, so claim returns nothing and process_one returns None.
The worker hands the leased job's parcel to the handler.
The update matched the job, the lease token and status leased, so one row changed.
No row matched the token because the lease expired and the job was claimed again; the worker drops its result.
The report command is a separate request; nothing in the worker triggers it.
After a job settles, run counts the ending and starts the next tick unless max_ticks is reached.
